scenes.heading: Building a scheduling system that avoids double-booking

sents.d: Building a scheduling system that avoids double-booking
A single source of truth for scheduling prevents costly conflicts.

Managing bookings across memory, texts, and scattered notes inevitably leads to double-bookings and missed appointments as job volume grows — a single scheduling system, even a simple shared calendar, prevents this.

Building in realistic buffer time between jobs (accounting for travel time and the likelihood that jobs run slightly long) reduces the cascading delays that come from back-to-back scheduling with zero slack.
Sending automatic or manual appointment reminders a day before reduces no-shows meaningfully, and is a low-effort addition once a scheduling system is in place.

take: Use one calendar, leave buffers and send reminders.
